Fat Malabsorption
Pathophysiology
Fat absorption may be impaired in liver disease. Possible causes 
include decreased bile salt secretion (as in PBC, sclerosing chol-
angitis, and biliary strictures), administration of medications 
such as cholestyramine, and pancreatic enzyme insufficiency. 
Stools may be greasy, floating, or light- or clay-colored, signify-
ing malabsorption, which can be verified by a 72-hour fecal fat 
study (see Chapter 28).
